description:
When sender and receiver are the same process nothing has to leave the heap. The BEAM special-cases this in erts_send_message with a data-less message struct. fz pushes the reference onto its own mailbox (already a GC root) and publishes it with Heap::mark_published_ref_aliased (runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:838-852), because the mailbox is a second holder and the in-place list rewrite guard (imp.rs:863-885, .agent/docs/pattern-matching.md:334-344) must see the spine as aliased.

Tests first:
- An adversarial fixture on all three paths: build a list, send it to self, append to it with a construction the compiler grants Rewrite permission, receive, assert the received list has the contents it had when sent. Show with list_retention telemetry (Process::list_retention_hits) that the rewrite path is actually exercised by the fixture; if no program can obtain Rewrite permission after a self-send, report exactly why (compiler rule, file:line) before deciding whether publication is still required.
- The fixture is seen to pass under today's deep copy, then fail under zero-copy without publication, then pass with it.

Done when:
- deep_copy_self_send_ref_for_aot (runtime/src/aot_shim.rs:504-510) and the JIT and interpreter self-send copies are deleted; the raw-pointer aliasing of one heap as both source and destination is gone.
- A self-send allocates zero bytes on the send path (alloc telemetry assertion in the fixture).
- Full gate green; pins reported, not edited. Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form; no co-author trailer.
title: A self-send is a mailbox push and a spine publication
